title: A record-initial whole points to the visible source
summary: Test whether a candidate record-initial whole is deictic to a visible panel, plant, or source location, rather than a generic opener. The prediction requires native owner evidence and held physical replication.

design.mechanism: The initial whole selects the external source currently being described.
design.unit: record-initial whole with native panel/source owner and subsequent record content
design.contrast: initial candidate versus matched non-deictic openers on panels with singular owners
design.prediction: At least 70% of candidate initial records resolve to the native source owner on held panels, exceeding opener controls by 25 points.
design.scope: admitted visual-owner spine and cached records; feasibility unknown because many apparent owners are proximity-only
design.countermodel: Initial forms are generic entry markers; owner resolution follows proximity or section frequency.
design.binding: independent native connector or diplomatic owner mapping on at least five physical folios
design.related: GDT699 deictic frame; GDT790 panel-owner overlay; no star-marker route is reopened
